Abstract We show that it is feasible to perform interactive isosurfacing of very large rectilinear datasets with brute-force ray tracing on a conventional (distributed) shared-memory multiprocessor machine. Rather than generate geometry representing the isosurface and ren-der with a z-buffer, for each pixel we trace a ray through a volume and do an analytic isosurface intersection computation ...
